fields.title: 1. Samsung Satellite Chip Report — The Boundary Between the Report and Primary Sources
fields.md:
### 1-1. What the Report Said

| Date | Outlet | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11/15 17:34 KST | Seoul Economic Daily (Koo Kyung-woo) | Samsung Foundry plans to secure 18nm FD-SOI capacity at its Austin fab to produce the STM32V8 for Starlink satellites. The process was co-developed with ST starting in 2014. Production currently takes place on ST's 300mm line in Crolles (France), and Austin production is expected around 2030. Total investment in Taylor and Austin is $37B. It cited an anonymous industry source, and there was no direct announcement from Samsung | ⑥ [Seoul Economic Daily 11/15](https://en.sedaily.com/business/2026/11/15/samsung-splits-texas-fabs-space-chips-in-austin-ai-chips-in) |
| 11/16 10:46 KST | Seoul Economic Daily (Kim So-yoon) | Same content. It wrote that Austin is the production base for Starlink satellite chips and Taylor is the 2nm production base for Tesla AI5 (2027) and AI6 (2028). There was no direct announcement from Samsung or SpaceX | ⑥ [Seoul Economic Daily 11/16](https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/11/16/samsung-wins-tesla-ai-chips-spacex-satellite-chips-in-us) |
| 11/16 | Wccftech, TipRanks, etc. | Repeated the Seoul Economic Daily report ('Reportedly') | ⑥ [Wccftech](https://wccftech.com/elon-musks-ties-with-samsung-deepen-as-the-korean-chip-giant-will-reportedly-make-chips-for-spacex-at-texas-says-report/) |

### 1-2. What the Primary Sources Say

| Source | Confirmed facts | Not confirmed | Source link |
|---|---|---|---|
| U.S. Department of Commerce CHIPS (NIST program page) | The final award to Samsung Austin Semiconductor is up to $4.745B, and it covers Taylor and Austin combined. The stated purpose of the Austin expansion is production of 'leading fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) process technologies', and the uses are 'aerospace, defense, and automotive'. 'All facilities are expected to be operational by 2030' | Austin's share of the amount · process node · customer (no mention of SpaceX or Starlink) | ③ [NIST](https://www.nist.gov/node/1855111) |
| STMicroelectronics announcement (2025-11-18) | The STM32V8 is built on an 18nm FD-SOI process with a Cortex-M85, up to 800MHz. SpaceX adopted it for the Starlink mini laser (inter-satellite laser link) system, and Nicolls (Starlink Engineering VP) commented. Broad availability is in Q1 2026 | Production site (the republished version does not mention Crolles or Samsung) · volume · amount | ⑥ [eeNews Europe 2025-11-22 republished version](https://www.eenewseurope.com/en/stm32v8-pushes-18nm-microcontroller-tech-into-new-performance-territory) — the original ST newsroom page could not be opened due to a tool error (473) |
| SpaceX filings | No related 8-K or IR | — | [EDGAR submissions](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json), accessed 2026-11-17 KST |

- **Summary**: Both the fact that Samsung is expanding FD-SOI at Austin and the fact that SpaceX uses FD-SOI-based ST chips are each confirmed by primary sources. The link that 'Samsung Austin makes chips for SpaceX' exists only in the report. The source is an anonymous industry insider with no company confirmation. The three-party structure, in which Samsung is the producer, ST is the customer contract counterparty, and SpaceX is the end user, is also the report's account (Source: table above).
- **Where it reaches the judgment layer**: Nowhere. This part is a microcontroller for the Starlink laser link. It is not an input to the satellite production milestone (Axis A) or the probability rules, and operation around 2030 falls outside the 12-month trigger window. Tesla AI5 and AI6 production at Taylor in the report is a Tesla matter, so it is not entered into the SpaceX judgment layer until the merger (T6) (Source: `state.milestones` · `state.probability_adjustment_rules`).
- **T17 newly added**: Starlink satellite chip supply chain. The checkpoints are ① official company confirmation ② Austin line operation ③ single-source risk factor in the SpaceX 10-K. The first checkpoint is the 12/01 monthly review (Source: `state.triggers_next_12m[T17]`).
- **Monitor's share (listing only)**: The monitor did not link this report to a trigger (—). This is the second supply-chain event, after T15 (solar cells) (Source: `state.open_questions_for_next_run`).
